I farm 7 mu here in Quzhou, same as my father did. Wheat in winter, maize in summer — this is what we always do. My two oldest help when they can but mostly it's me and my wife. The third one works in Handan city now.

Last year I got about 500 kg of wheat per mu and around 600 kg of maize. Not bad. I will do similar this year. No need to change much when it worked.

For wheat, I plant Jimai variety — the seed dealer in town sells it, most neighbors use it too. I plough the land once before sowing in October. For fertilizer, I use one bag of compound fertilizer (diammonium, 50 kg) per mu before planting, then top-dress with urea in spring when wheat starts growing again — about 20 kg urea per mu. That gives me roughly 18 kg N, 12 kg P, and a little K. I water 3 times — before winter, at jointing, and at grain filling. The well is there, water is not the big worry. I spray once for aphids and once for rust if I see it — so 2 sprays.

For maize after wheat harvest in June, I don't plough — no time. I use rotary tiller and plant directly. Zhengdan or Xianyu hybrid seed, whatever the dealer has. One bag compound fertilizer at planting, then 25 kg urea at big trumpet stage. That's maybe 20 kg N, 10 kg P. I water 2 times if rain is short. Spray once for corn borer.

I would rather put a little extra urea than lose yield. Fertilizer costs money but losing half the harvest is much worse.
